name: Jade
physical: Traditionally associated with long life and wellbeing
Said to bring a balanced, restful feeling
Folk tradition links it with comfort in the kidneys and lower back
summary: Jade is the treasured green stone of East Asia and Mesoamerica, associated with luck, harmony, wisdom and protection through thousands of years of tradition.
intro: Jade is the name given to two different stones, jadeite and nephrite, that share a tough, smooth, waxy character and a love of green. Both are dense interlocking masses of tiny crystals, which makes them extraordinarily difficult to break, a property that made them ideal for early tools and later for fine carvings. Colours range from white and lavender to apple green and a deep forest tone. Cool and smooth to hold, a polished jade piece has a heft that feels reassuring. It is among the best-loved stones in the world, treasured for its beauty, its toughness and its extraordinarily rich cultural history.
history: In China jade, called yu, has been carved for at least seven thousand years, and was symbolically linked with virtue, moral integrity and immortality. The Confucian tradition compared a gentleman's character to the stone, and burial suits of jade plaques were made for Han dynasty nobility. In Mesoamerica the Olmec and Maya prized blue-green jadeite for masks and ornaments, valuing it above gold. The Maori of New Zealand carved pounamu, a nephrite, into treasured heirlooms known as hei-tiki. The word jade comes from the Spanish piedra de ijada, meaning stone of the flank, a reflection of an old belief about its effects. Today it remains a cherished gemstone worldwide.
meaning: Crystal practitioners regard jade as a stone of harmony, good fortune and quiet wisdom. It is said to bring a settled, friendly atmosphere to the home, to support honest dealings and to encourage generosity. In Chinese tradition it is also a protective stone, worn as bangles and pendants to guard travelling or children. Green jade is linked with the heart chakra and with growth, prosperity and patient success, while white and lavender jade suggest purity and gentle intuition. Many people use it as a calm anchor, a stone to touch when emotions run high. Physically it is traditionally associated with long life, balance and comfort in the lower back, though it is a symbol of wellbeing rather than a treatment.
howToUse: Wear a jade bangle or pendant as a daily talisman, or carry a smooth pebble to rub between your fingers when tension rises. In feng shui, place a jade plant carving or a stone in the east or south-east for family and wealth. Keep a piece in the kitchen or near the front door to encourage a harmonious household. During meditation, rest a stone on the heart and breathe slowly. Gift jade to mark a birth, a wedding or a new home as a wish for good fortune.
care: Jade is tough and water-safe, so a rinse in lukewarm water with a soft cloth is enough for cleaning. Avoid harsh chemicals, steam and ultrasonic cleaners, which can damage treated stones. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or brief sunlight. Wearing jade next to skin is traditionally thought to improve its lustre. Store it away from harder gems like diamond and sapphire, and keep carved pieces wrapped in soft cloth to avoid knocks.
identify: Real jade feels cool, heavy and smooth, with a fine, even grain and a waxy to glassy glow. It does not show bubbles or swirl marks, and a tap produces a clear ringing tone. Many items sold as jade are dyed quartzite, serpentine, aventurine, glass or resin. Jadeite may be bleached and polymer-impregnated, known as B-jade, or dyed, C-jade. For valuable pieces seek a gemological report that states whether the stone is natural A-grade material.

faq.q: What is the difference between jadeite and nephrite?
faq.a: Both are called jade. Jadeite is a sodium aluminium pyroxene, rarer and often more vividly coloured, while nephrite is a tough amphibole rock in softer greens and creams. Both have a long carving history.

Jade is traditionally associated with luck, harmony, longevity and moral integrity. In Chinese culture it is the most revered stone, and in other traditions it stands for protection and peaceful prosperity.

faq.q: How can I tell real jade from fake?
faq.a: Real jade feels cool and heavy, with a fine grain and no bubbles. Fakes are often dyed quartzite, serpentine or glass. A reputable seller or gem lab can confirm material and treatments for valuable pieces.
